evidence_notes: CVE-2022-39207: Structured CVE input confirms user-uploaded artifact file flows through ContentDetector.detectMediaType into Content-Type response header, enabling uploaded HTML to execute in the application origin — source-to-sink path is complete.
Patch adb6e314: Fix removes ContentDetector, adds X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, and sets Content-Type to MimeTypes.OCTET_STREAM — confirms the exact missing guard and safe fix semantics.
Reviewer notes confirm this is a deliberate correction from the prior mech_template_expression_untrusted_eval attribution; the evidence does not support template/expression evaluation.
main_issue: The mechanism is coherent and well-supported by the reviewed evidence: source (artifact download resource serving uploaded files), sink (Content-Type header derived from ContentDetector on attacker-controlled bytes), missing guard (no nosniff, no forced inert type), exploit precondition (attacker uploads HTML/JS, victim opens link), and safe fix (octet-stream + nosniff) all align cleanly. The single representative case (CVE-2022-39207) is sufficient to establish the mechanism, but the boundary family has only one confirmed member, which limits cross-case coherence validation.
mechanism_name: user-uploaded artifact served with sniffed active content type
